Where Claude Haiku falls behind Opus: 163 coding runs with hidden tests

Measured and written by Jonhisking · Updated 2026-10-25. Disclosure: TokenSave gets no funding, credits or sponsorship from AI companies. All measurements use our own paid subscriptions.

On every coding task with a clear spec, Claude Haiku 5.5 matched Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5: full marks on all 21 runs each, from a five-level game to a spreadsheet engine with cycle detection. The gap showed up on a real bug in the marked Markdown parser. No run fixed it completely, but Sonnet passed 6 of the maintainers’ 7 test cases in 8 of 10 runs and Opus in 6 of 10, Haiku in 1 of 10. Letting the agents run the test suite did not change that. Fewer runs broke other code with tests (2 of 15 without, 0 of 15 with), but that gap is too small to rule out chance. Haiku cost about 94% less per run than Opus at API prices.

Measured 2026-10-23 to 2026-10-24 · 163 runs (+11 excluded) · Claude Code 2.1.295, Codex CLI 0.162/0.163, Antigravity CLI 1.4.5 · License CC BY 4.0

DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23600477 · Also on Hugging Face · Kaggle · GitHub

Key findings

  • Levels 2 to 5 (apps from a spec, or an existing app to fix): Haiku, Sonnet and Opus 21/21 runs with full marks each, Antigravity + Gemini 4 Argon 18/18, Codex 17/20 (one syntax error from literal \n in a file, one app whose fixed category list and −$ amounts failed three checks, one missed report row).
  • Level 5A was a brownfield task: a 1,032-line budget app with six planted bugs described only by symptoms, plus three features. Every Claude run fixed all six bugs, added all three features and kept all 23 earlier tests passing.
  • Level 6, real bugs in marked: the easy one (a one-line regular expression) and the medium one were solved by almost every run, Haiku and Sonnet in 14 to 20 seconds.
  • The hard bug is where the models split. A backslash at the end of a code span hid emphasis later in the line. Every run fixed the examples in the bug report; the cases left were code spans that themselves contain a backtick (such as _``\`_``), which the report did not mention and the maintainers covered in their test. Cases passed per run, without tests: Haiku 5, 5, 5, 5, 5; Sonnet 6, 6, 5, 6, 6; Opus 6, 6, 6, 5, marked no longer loads; Codex 3, 3, 4, 4, 4; Gemini 3, 3, 3 (the unfixed code passes 3).
  • Running the tests did not close the gap. In 15 more Claude runs the dependencies were installed and the prompt allowed running node and marked’s spec suite; every one of them ran the suite and checked its own examples. Cases passed: Haiku 5, 6, 5, 5, 5; Sonnet 6, 6, 6, 5, 6; Opus 6, 6, 5, 5, 6. The only visible difference was damage: without tests one Haiku run broke 15 other spec tests and one Opus run left an invalid regular expression that stopped marked from loading at all; with tests no run broke anything. With 15 runs each, that could be chance.
  • What this means in practice: with a clear spec, Haiku is enough (same full marks as Opus at about 94% less per run). For a real bug whose report leaves cases out, Sonnet or Opus caught the extra edge case far more often (8 and 6 of 10 runs vs 1 of 10); on this bug Sonnet did best and cost less than Opus, but with 10 runs each that gap could be chance. Running tests did not find the missing case; no run with tests broke other code, but there are too few runs to credit the tests for that. And still review edge cases yourself: no model fixed the bug completely.
  • Cost per run at API prices (Claude Code’s own figure): Haiku $0.026, Sonnet $0.19, Opus $0.45 on average over all levels. Codex and Antigravity ran on subscription plans and report no price.
  • Antigravity’s headless mode ends a turn at the first denied command. With read-only allow-rules, several Gemini runs stopped before editing (a node -e line with quotes needs an exact rule on Windows). With full permissions Gemini solved the easy and medium bugs too, but took 2 to 11 minutes, and one hard run used its whole 30-minute limit without an edit.

The hard bug: test cases passed per run

The maintainers’ test for this fix has 7 cases; the unfixed code passes 3. “Tests allowed”: dependencies preinstalled, the prompt allowed running node and the spec suite, and Claude Code could run node, npm test/run and read-only git. Codex was also run with tests allowed, but its Windows sandbox blocked the build in all 5 runs, so those runs are excluded; Gemini had used up its quota.

The tasks

  • L2: a five-level brick game with pause, a level-skip key and saved level and best score (9 checks, played in headless Chromium).
  • L3: a multi-file expense tracker with CSV and summary modules (12 checks).
  • L4: a budget app with five modules (CSV with line breaks, ranges, monthly repeats with month ends, budgets, 50-step undo) and three hash-routed views (23 checks).
  • L5A: the L4 app written by one of the Gemini runs (8 files, 1,032 lines) with six planted bugs reported only as user symptoms, plus three new features (38 checks, including the 23 L4 tests as regression tests). Because Gemini wrote the starting code, it may have had a small advantage.
  • L5B: a spreadsheet engine and page: precedence with unary minus and right-associative ^, eight functions, six error values, cycle detection and recovery, relative and $absolute copy, undo, CSV (38 checks, 32 of them calling the engine directly).
  • L6: three bugs fixed in marked in September and October 2026 (commits 123ce04b, cc07bb9c and 6a57018f). Each run started from the commit before the fix with a symptom-only bug report; we copied back only its src/ folder, then ran the upstream fix’s spec file and marked’s full spec suite (about 1,900 checks).

Method

  • One Windows 11 laptop, each run in a fresh folder. Claude Code 2.1.295 (-p, effort medium, acceptEdits), Codex CLI 0.162 (exec, medium, workspace-write sandbox), Antigravity CLI 1.4.5 (-p, gemini-4-argon-medium, accept-edits with read-only allow-rules; full permissions for the level 6 re-run).
  • Every checker was validated before the runs: a reference solution scores full marks and deliberately broken versions lose exactly their target checks. Runs were scored twice where a check depends on timing.
  • We stopped L5A after 4 rounds and L5B after 2 because every run scored full marks. L6 easy and medium have 2 runs per tool; the hard bug has 5 runs per tool without tests (Gemini 3) and 5 per Claude model with tests allowed (measured 2026-10-24).

Limitations

  • Few runs per cell at levels 2 to 5 (1 to 5). The split between models rests on one hard bug from one project, 10 runs per Claude model.
  • The prompts list every element id and function name the tests use, which makes levels 2 to 5 easier than real work.
  • The tools differ in more than the model: Codex can run commands in its sandbox, Claude Code in acceptEdits cannot run shell commands unless allowed, Antigravity stops on a denied command.
  • The tests-allowed comparison covers the three Claude models only: Codex’s Windows sandbox stopped esbuild from building marked, and Gemini was out of quota.
